propositions: The false_accept metric computes specificity (true-negative rate, higher-is-better) but is consumed at two sites as an error rate (lower-is-better), causing inverted comparison logic.
A candidate that false-fires on fewer safe items than baseline is incorrectly failed by the non-inferiority rise check at parity.py:125 due to the inverted metric.
The max_false_accept ceiling of 0.10 is effectively always-fail because the old computation yields values above 0.9 for any competent gate.

Correcting the false_accept computation from (not-blocked safe items) to (blocked safe items) aligns parity.py with the established definition in eval.py and resolves all comparison directions without operator changes.
A gold fixture in fidelity_spot_eval.py mislabelled safe items as advisory while the inline comment stated they must be blocked, a contradiction that was only survivable under the inverted metric.
